t: Performance: all street-lamp lenses share one shader (three.js r187 material instances), so loading compiles 3 fewer shaders

Map: Ciudad Nueva is now a big city island, about 2.6 x 1.3 km: the old downtown plus five new districts on a street grid (Puerto's warehouses and docks, Lumang Bayan's bahay na bato and chapels, Bagong Bayan's shophouses and towers, San Roque with parks and fountains, Silangan's houses), the Altavista hills with a loop road, villas and a lookout, and Baybayin Beach with resorts, cottages, stalls, a malecon and a lighthouse
Map: Isla Kambal, a twin-peaked island between the main island and the city, with a loop road, a lookout and bridges to both, so there is a second way into the city

Map: Atol Perlas, a crescent atoll with a lagoon east of Bato: causeway from Bato, bridge to Silangan, a resort, cottages and a lighthouse; and Tatlong Buhangin, three palm sandbars off the old quarter

Faster: island coastlines use a cached distance field (the terrain no longer walks every outline point for every vertex), deep sea-bed terrain tiles are not built at all, and walking / the on-foot camera only test collision boxes near you instead of all of them
Map: five hilltop lookout towers (Bundok Alon, the pass, the east coast, the west coast and the east islet), tall enough to steer by, with a beacon that glows at night
Map: Talon Falls, a waterfall pouring off the volcano's flank into a plunge pool at the head of the river, between gorge walls
Map: Fuerte Viejo, a ruined stone fort west of the volcano, and a giant balete tree on the east coast
Map: roadside rest stops with a shed, benches and a campfire on the long empty roads (west, north and east)
Particles: sparks from pegs in a hard lean, from scraping a wall and from a crash slide on tarmac; backfire pops and crackle on the overrun; exhaust puffs on high-rpm upshifts; cold-start vapour
Particles: clods and gravel thrown off a spinning tyre on dirt and grass, a dust ring on hard jump landings
Particles: campfire flames and embers, waterfall mist and spray, volcano steam, falling balete leaves, fireflies over the rice paddies and terraces at night

Engine: three.js updated from r186 to r187 (newer WebGPU/WebGL renderer fixes: BatchedMesh sort and draw-range fixes, sharper environment lighting, faster shader builds). The game should look and run the same; the first load downloads the new library once.

Performance (WebGPU): the static town is recorded into render bundles once and replayed every frame instead of being re-submitted object by object, which cuts the CPU time of drawing a frame (the biggest cost in the phone benchmark). Bundles are culled by area, and a part is re-recorded only when something in it changes (distance culling, night lights, the lamp level). New switch in Options > Graphics > Advanced: Render bundles (on by default; turn it off to compare in the benchmark). The draw-call counter includes bundled draws.

Performance (from a phone benchmark): with FXAA on, the frame it smooths is now kept in 8-bit colour with no depth buffer instead of 16-bit float plus depth, a third of the memory traffic for that full-screen pass every frame, with no visible change. Night light pools, lamp halos and mission rings/beams are drawn once instead of twice per frame (three.js drew every see-through two-sided object twice). Benchmark verdict: the switched-off phases are compared with the reference drifting linearly from the first to the last run (a warming phone no longer shows a feature costing negative time), CPU and GPU both near the limit is called that, and a CPU-heavy frame says how much of it is the draw stage.

Honda Click125, matched to a side photo: the muffler sits further back and angles up to an alloy end plate, the seat is thicker with its nose hanging over the tunnel, the handlebar cover is a lower, more compact wedge with the meter on its back face, the plate hanger is a thin stalk reaching down and back, and the wheels have the real 5 split Y spokes.

Honda Click125: checked against a straight side photo. The seat and rear body now sweep up to the tail like the real scooter (grab bar, tail lamp and rear signals moved up with it, and the passenger sits on the higher seat), and there is a black belly under the floorboard.
Honda Click125: the pointed nose is a little smaller.

Honda Click125: the front now juts forward like the real scooter. The upper cowl slopes down from the handlebars to a pointed nose over the front wheel, with a black V on top, the twin LED headlamps and light strips on the nose, and a big body-colour front fender with its own pointed tip.

Bikes now show their latest real-world look (from new research on the Philippine models; the Rusi Macho is unchanged). Honda Click125: the 2026 facelift, with open ducts in the side fairings, a one-piece grab bar and a 3D "Click" badge. The paints are now the 2026 range (Pearl Arctic White, Pearl Sylvestris Gray, Obsidian Black Metallic, and the matte Smart Edition in Mat Axis Gray or Mat Fresco Brown, with gold badges).

Yamaha Aerox: the 2025 all-new model, with an XMAX-style headlamp pod and twin LED lamps, a carbon-look chin and inner-fairing trim, a pointed LED tail lamp with the signals sticking out at the sides, and a rear disc. Paints: Race Blue, Glaze Blue and Yamaha Black, plus the SP in Matte Blue with red trim, red stitching and red wheels.

Suzuki Raider R150: the MY2026 look, with winglets on the front shrouds, a full-LED headlamp and black wheels. Paints: Pearl Bright Ivory, Candy Matte Bordeaux Red, Metallic Matte Fibroin Gray, Metallic Medium Blue and Shadow Solid Black.

Yamaha NMAX 155: a slim 2025 LED tail lamp and gold wheel trim on the Tech MAX. Paints are the Philippine range: Black, Light Grey, Dark Magma, Sword Gray and Ceramic Gray. Yamaha XMAX 300 paints: Ceramic Gray, Sword Gray, Icon Black and Dark Magma.

Smash Fi: an engine heat guard, and the Fi paints (Candy Summer Red, Titan Black, Metallic Matte Stellar Blue). Rouser NS125 Fi: twin LED strip tail lamps, in Bright Yellow or Sparkling Black. TMX Supremo: Candy Ruby Red or Fiery Black. CBR650R: adds the 2026 Matt Gunpowder Black with a yellow fairing accent. Ninja H2: paints now carry Kawasaki's names.

Buildings you can go into: the new Tambayan Billiards & Bar across the road from the parking lot (pink BILLIARDS neon over the door). Walk up to the door and tap ENTER: two pool tables under green lamps, a bar counter with stools and a bottle shelf, a jukebox, a tv showing the PBA, round tables, ceiling fans and regulars (a bartender wiping the counter, people with a drink at the bar and the tables, someone lining up a shot). EXIT at the door takes you back out.

Shops and things to drink: ORDER at the counter (ginbilog, beer, a litro of strong beer, softdrinks, water, sisig, chicharon); sari-sari stores now sell at their front door (BUY). You start with ₱300 and the fares from giving pedestrians a ride go into the same wallet. What you buy is in your hands: the on-foot button becomes DRINK / EAT.

Drunk: one ginbilog is plenty. You stagger, sway, can't sprint, the stick turns under you; the screen wobbles, swims and splits into a drifting double image and the horizon tilts. And you can't ride at all: the steering is mostly the gin's (with stretches where the bars go the wrong way), the throttle surges and dies on its own and the brake gets grabbed. Fighting it doesn't help. It wears off in about three minutes; kape, water and sisig help.

Billiards: walk up to a table and SHOOT (the cue ball goes away from where you stand; the first shot breaks the rack). Balls click, bank and drop, a scratch comes back on the spot, RACK when the table is clear. Drunk, your aim wanders.

Friends: tap a friend's name tag while either of you is on foot to WAVE, TREAT them to a drink (you pay, it lands in their hands), CHEERS (you both drink: tagay!) or CALL them over (your spot, or the bar you're in, becomes their waypoint from anywhere). MULTIPLAYER in the menu now lists everyone with where they are (riding, on foot, which building) and FIND / CALL buttons. Friends in the same building see each other inside, and a drunk friend sways. The relay needs redeploying for these (server/README.md).

One on-foot button for everything: GET ON, ENTER, EXIT, ORDER, BUY, SHOOT, DRINK, whichever is nearest (F or E on a keyboard). The walking camera no longer ends up inside a building's walls when you back up to one.
Interiors, shops, items and their effects are data (data/interiors.json, data/shop.json): a new room, item or shop is an entry there.

Particles: tyre smoke from burnouts, wheelspin and locked wheels on tarmac, dust kicked up off-road, a dust trail when a crash slides, and a splash when you ride into the sea. One small pool drawn in a single call and animated on the GPU, so it costs nothing while no smoke is in the air; fewer puffs on Low quality.

Pedestrians: people now walk the sidewalks of every road and do everyday things. Sando boys hang out, squat and chat, people walk their dogs (the dog sniffs, sits and waits on a leash), students in school uniforms with backpacks and ties head about, and titas, lolos, office workers, joggers and tambays fill in the rest. They go in and out of buildings' front doors, cross the street, jump out of the way of a fast bike, sit down dazed if you clip one, and wave when you walk past.

Give a ride: some people wave you down (yellow marker above them). Stop next to one on a bike with a free seat and they hop on behind you (or into the sidecar); a front door somewhere on the island, a house, a store, the church, becomes the drop-off. Stop there and they walk inside. Fares and rides given are kept on your phone.
Options > Game > Pedestrians: Off / Few / Normal / Busy. Normal follows your graphics quality; there are fewer people at night.

One character system for everybody: you on foot, your friends' walkers, the pedestrians, their dogs and your passenger share one body (the rider's look) and one pose library. Walking on foot is now animated (arms and legs swing in step, a tuck when you jump).

Built for phones: the whole crowd is one draw call (poses and outfits are worked out on the GPU), only people in view are drawn, far ones think less often, nobody casts into the shadow map, and the crowd lives in a ring around you instead of everywhere at once.
Who the people are is data (data/npc.json): a new kind of person is a new entry with its outfit colours, parts, activities and lines, no code.

MSAA: the 4-sample colour buffer is no longer written back to memory after the scene is drawn (only the smoothed result is ever read). On phones this saves tens of megabytes of memory traffic a frame; without motion blur the 4-sample depth buffer is dropped the same way.

Benchmark: a phase now measures for its full time once frames have settled. Switching post-processing off makes the game build its shaders again, which on a phone took most of that phase and left only a fraction of a second (12 frames) to measure, so its cost came out wrong (even negative). A phase that never settles is marked CUT SHORT and left out of the verdict.

Benchmark: hitches are now judged per event (how often the frame after a shadow refresh or dash upload hitches, against frames with no event), which is fair for the dash upload that only happens in first person.

New benchmark: Options > System > Benchmark reloads the game, then rides a fixed route for about a minute and a half and records frame times, CPU time per stage, GPU time (where the device has a GPU timer), draw calls and every hitch with what came just before it (shadow-map refresh, dash upload, memory cleanup, sky update). It then repeats one stretch with shadow-map updates, post-processing and resolution switched off to price each, and once more at the end to catch the phone slowing down as it heats up. The report is plain text in the same tab, with a Copy report button.
Fixed: the first frame after PLAY could carry a negative time step on a slow load, which froze the bike's physics for as long as the load had blocked the screen (up to a couple of seconds).

WebGPU (and WebGL on GPUs without multi-draw): street-lamp halos are no longer drawn in daylight. They were invisible by day (opacity 0) but still drawn as blended quads, about 15 draws a frame for nothing. They come back as before when the lamps switch on at sunset.

WebGPU (most phones on recent Chrome): GPU-culled props now cast shadows from their own shadow-only copy holding just the props around the bike. Before, every shadow-map refresh (about every 8 m of riding) re-drew every visible prop out to the draw distance, and every frame drew the ring of shadow casters behind the camera too. Shadows look the same; the periodic GPU spike on shadow refreshes is much smaller.

Engine-sound effects of air filters, carbs and throttle bodies, head work, valve springs and ECU / CDI / tune options now live on each part option in the bike data, so new parts can change the sound without code changes. Sound is unchanged, except that a racing CDI and an engine tune now stack their crackle and roughness instead of only the bigger one counting.

Engine sound is now worked out from each bike's real engine: bore, stroke, compression ratio and peak-power rpm set the exhaust header (A. Graham Bell's tuned-length and diameter formulas), the muffler (a Helmholtz resonator) and the intake runner (the tuned-runner formula), so every bike's note comes from its own hardware.

The header now rings like a real pipe (odd harmonics, rising in pitch as the exhaust gas heats up under load), each exhaust pulse lasts a fixed crank angle so it gets shorter and sharper as the revs climb, the muffler sound is radiated the way a real tailpipe radiates it, valve clatter follows mean piston speed and combustion knock follows compression.

Parts change the physics instead of a volume knob: bore-up kits add displacement, high-compression pistons raise the compression ratio, racing cams open the exhaust earlier (harder bark, lumpier idle), slip-ons shrink the muffler, full systems fit a tuned-length header (lower, deeper pipe note) and open pipes drop the muffler entirely.
Engine sound upgrade: idle is no longer a steady drone. Each firing varies a little in strength and timing and the idle speed hunts gently, more so on rough singles, less on smooth multis.

Tuning is now clearly audible: a racing cam gives a lumpy, loping idle and more valvetrain clatter; air filters, big throttle bodies and carbs add induction roar; a bore-up thumps deeper and harder; a lightened flywheel sounds choppier and a heavy one smoother; race ECU maps, CDIs and tunes crackle more on the overrun; exhausts step up more in volume, bass and rasp.
Valve tick is now heard at idle too, where you notice it most on a real bike.
Engine voice costs about 30% less audio-thread time.
Garage ENGINE tab now has a sub-menu: Intake & fuel, Head, Bottom end, Ignition, Exhaust and ECU & tuning, each with a count of what you've changed there.

New engine parts, only where they fit the real engine: big-bore throttle body and high-flow injector (fuel-injected singles), Keihin PE24 / PE28 carburettors, ignition coil and racing CDI (TMX and Macho; coil on the Smash), racing valve springs, ported head, forged high-compression piston, bore-up kit (fuel-injected singles; the carb bikes keep theirs under Engine tune), and engine oil for every bike. Cams now move the power up the rev range instead of adding it everywhere.

New DYNO tab: strap the bike to an inertia drum and do a full-throttle pull, with the engine sound following the revs. Pick the gear (CVTs shift by themselves), keep up to 5 runs on one chart with a stock ghost, and read rear-wheel PS and Nm with their rpm, loss below the brochure figure and the gain against your first run. A light flywheel reads higher on the drum, a heavy one lower, like on a real one.
Engine internals are no longer sent to other players (they can't be seen), so they don't count against the 24-part multiplayer limit.

New garage parts, each fitted only to bikes it really suits: spark plug (iridium, not on the CBR650R or H2 which come with one), racing camshaft (the small singles), lithium battery (all bikes, about 1 to 2 kg lighter), clutch (heavy-duty springs on every geared bike, plus a slipper clutch kit for the Raider R150), chain (X-ring, and a 520 race conversion for the CBR650R and H2), and for the scooters racing clutch shoes and a racing drive belt.
Steel-braided brake lines for the bikes with hydraulic disc brakes (not the drum-braked TMX, Macho and Smash).
The garage shows what a clutch or chain/belt part changes (clutch hold, drive efficiency, slipper clutch).

Fix Ciudad Nueva: widening it east pushed the Bato bridge deck over the new avenues and buildings, lifting streets above the houses next to them. The city now grows west and south only (about 45% wider to the west, 27% deeper, new avenues, a south street, 11 more towers) and the bridge lands as before.
New buildings on Isla Bantay are no longer placed on top of roads (a cottage on the west bridge, a shop on the lake loop, huts on the cape road).

New: Isla Bantay, a big crescent island that wraps the whole north half of the main island across a 110 m channel, reached by three bridges (west, north with cable pylons, east). A scenic coast highway runs its full length with esses. Along it: Bundok Alon (a mountain range), Laguna Bughaw (a lake with a lakeside loop road), Talampas Mesa (spiral road up a flat-topped mesa with a circuit on top), Kalbaryo Badlands (rocky off-road field), Cabo Hangin (spiral road up a cliff to a lighthouse), jungle hills, and beach resorts and fishing villages at the tips.
Ciudad Nueva is bigger, with more avenues, a southern street and more towers.
The map grows from about 2.2 km to 3.1 km across. Extra islands can now set a coarser outline step and fewer palms, and palms no longer sprout along the seams between joined island pieces.

Fewer GPU hitches: the shadow map is redrawn about 4x less often. It now sits ahead of the camera and re-centres every 8 m instead of every 3 m, snapped to its own texel grid so shadow edges stay still, and it no longer redraws every 2 s while parked just because the sun crept a fraction of a degree.

The first-person dashboard no longer rebuilds its mipmaps on every refresh (on WebGPU that was 9 extra render passes up to 10 times a second), and it never refreshes in the same frame as a shadow redraw.
The sky is drawn after the ground and buildings, so it is only shaded where you can actually see it instead of over the whole screen first.

Fixed the FPS readout being cut off: the box was sized for the old short text, so physics time, draws, the cpu line and the hitch meter were clipped. It now shows up to four lines (API and fps, physics, draws and resolution, cpu, hitches) and the layout reserves room for them.
More LOD: nipa huts drop their stilts past ~110 m (60 vertices instead of 204), and the terrain gets a fourth, 40 m detail level past 900 m (High graphics draw distance).

WebGPU gets the palm and tree LOD too: the GPU culling pass now sends each palm and rainforest tree to either its full-detail or its low-detail version by distance (past ~160 m), so WebGPU draws about a third as many palm vertices at a typical spot, like WebGL 2 since 11.65.

Performance round for the bigger map: palms and rainforest trees switch to low-detail versions past ~110 m (about a third fewer triangles per frame, same draw calls), road pieces past the draw distance are no longer drawn, and the island builds faster at load (terrain generation about 3x quicker, same terrain).

Big map expansion. Ciudad Nueva: a city island south of the main island with a street grid, glass towers up to 32 floors (lit windows at night), a plaza, church and market. Ocean highway: a 750 m arched cable-stayed bridge (two 38 m pylons) sweeping from the south-east coast over open sea to the city, with a ramp down to Isla Bato. New islets: Isla Bato (rock-garden off-road island with boulders), Parola Peak (a cone island with a spiral road up to a lighthouse), Stunt Atoll (kickers, a bowl and a loop track) and a pier from the old islet to the city. Off-road: Batuhan Rocks and Bukirin Whoops, ridged rocky bumpy terrain with boulders. Underground: the Underground River Cave, a sunken roofed rock hall with two mouths, a skylight, pillars, stalagmites, glowing crystals and a pool. Map tech: new hill and rough terrain features, road points with heights and a bridge flag (deck over open water leaves the sea floor alone), tower and cave buildings, map labels on any feature, terrain grid now follows the bounding box of all land.

Four weirder hub challenges: Roguelite run (lime R: endless floors of random mini trials, three hearts, and after every floor you ride through one of three coloured doors to pick a perk: more time, a heart, a magnet or a shield), Speed bomb (red X: arms at 50 km/h and blows up if you stay slow, ride to the halo to defuse it), Meteor storm (white M: warning halos flash on the ground and strike a moment later, stay out of them for 40 s) and Catch the hare (indigo H: a glowing hare dashes over the island, stay in its halo to catch it, it comes back faster).

Four new hub challenges on the same halos: Gate rush (gold G: thread a chain of 8 gates, each buys time), Orb rush (cyan O: grab 10 orbs around the hub before the clock runs out), Speed trap (orange S: hit the halo flat out, beat your record per bike) and Stunt run (purple T: wheelies, stoppies and jumps score points for 45 s with a growing combo). Hubs now roll across all six job types.

The browser's own right-click / touch-and-hold menu is switched off everywhere (game, menus, garage, map): no context menu, no link or image drag, no text-selection handles or magnifier. Name, room code and server fields still allow paste.

The XMAX 300 is rebuilt from reference photos instead of being a stretched NMAX: tall angular painted side shields over a narrow dark face with slim twin headlamps, a painted panel beside the front wheel and a sharp painted fin along the bottom, two-tone rear body with a grilled dark lower panel, tall clear windscreen, handlebar on the fork top with long mirror stalks, split grab rails, exposed twin shock springs, black muffler with a silver end cap and 5 split-spoke wheels. Paints follow the PH colours: Light Gray (bronze wheels), Matte Dark Gray, Red, Black.

New bike: Yamaha XMAX 300 (PH 2023), the NMAX's big brother, with Yamaha's published numbers: 292 cc liquid-cooled Blue Core single, 28 PS @ 7,250 rpm, 29 Nm @ 5,750, 183 kg, 1,540 mm wheelbase, 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheels, 267 / 245 mm discs with ABS, traction control, smart key. Plain belt CVT (no YECVT or Stop & Start): 0-100 km/h in about 9.7 s, top about 137 km/h. It is built by the NMAX's model code one size up, with its own twin headlamps, X-shaped tail lamp, 10-spoke wheels, taller screen and an amber-accent colour TFT. Takes a pillion like every bike; its sidecar mount data is in place for when the sidecar option comes back.
The sidecar option is hidden again on every bike except the TMX Supremo and Macho 125 (the other bikes keep their sidecar mount data, ready to switch on later).

Every bike can now take the tricycle sidecar: fit it under Parts on any of the ten bikes. The sidecar is no longer tied to the TMX and Macho models; each bike's data file says where the sidecar's struts bolt to its frame, and the sidecar centres itself on that bike's wheelbase. The sidecar also no longer shares the model-variant slot, so it combines freely with other parts that change the model (H2R kit, Tech MAX, Smash wheels).
Bike card class labels (SCOOTER, SPORT, ...) now come from each bike's data file.

Speed blur gets San Andreas-style ghost trails and a speed vignette. Above 60 km/h a fading echo of the last frames trails behind the fast-moving road edges and roadside (the faster a spot streaks, the stronger its trail), while the point you are heading for and your bike stay crisp; the screen edges dim and lose a little colour as speed builds. The strength slider sets both the streak length and how long the trails linger. Phone-friendly: the trails are kept at half resolution and add one small pass, and nothing extra runs below 60 km/h.

Motion blur is now speed blur in the style of GTA San Andreas: it only appears when you ride fast (fades in from 60 km/h, full at 130), never on foot. Looking around, leaning, turning and the camera swinging no longer blur anything: the streaks come only from how far the camera travelled, so they fan out from the point you are heading for and the horizon stays sharp.

Motion blur (Options > Graphics > Look, on by default, with a strength slider). The world streaks as you ride, like a camera shutter; your own bike and rider stay sharp. Built for phones: the streak is gathered from a half-resolution Kawase-blurred copy of the frame (two small passes), so a few samples give a smooth trail, and it switches itself off (no extra passes) whenever the view is not moving.

First person: the Ninja H2 and NMAX 155 gauges are visible again. The H2 meter sat inside the solid windscreen; it now sits on the screen's rider-side face. The NMAX meter hood peaked at the back and, with the handlebar riser cover, hid the display; the hood now has its visor edge at the front and the display is a little larger.

New bike: Yamaha NMAX 155 (2025), with Yamaha's published numbers: 155 cc liquid-cooled VVA single, 15.4 PS @ 8,000 rpm, 14.2 Nm @ 6,500, 1,340 mm wheelbase, 13-inch wheels, 230 mm discs front and rear with dual-channel ABS, traction control, Stop & Start. Modelled after the black PH unit: X-shaped LED face, tall smoked screen, flat floorboard, boomerang side panel, copper-tank twin shocks.

Two variants in the garage DRIVE tab. Standard: belt CVT with rollers, springs and pulley to tune. Tech MAX: Yamaha's electronic CVT (YECVT) with T and S modes (S keeps the revs ~1,000 rpm higher) and the 3-level Y-Shift: tap ▼ (Q) for more revs and more engine braking, ▲ (E) to step back; it drops out by itself when you brake or let go of the throttle. The Tech MAX also gets a colour TFT showing the mode and Y-Shift level.
Scooters with an electronic CVT get ▲▼ buttons above the brake pad on touch screens. Scooter brake pads now say ABS instead of CBS on bikes that have ABS.

Gearboxes now follow each bike's owner's manual. The Honda TMX Supremo has its real five-down pattern: neutral is at the top, every upshift is a press (N-1-2-3-4-5), and a downshift from 1st goes to neutral, even while rolling. The other manual bikes keep 1 down, rest up, and the Smash stays a 4-speed rotary.
Suzuki Raider R150 Fi: real FI gear ratios (taller overall, 6th is now an overdrive). It no longer hits the limiter in 6th and tops out around 138 km/h instead of 125.
The garage DRIVE stats now show the number of gears, the shift pattern and the primary ratio.

New bike: Kawasaki Ninja H2. 998 cc supercharged inline-four with 231 PS, Kawasaki's published gear ratios, weights and dimensions, a green trellis frame, single-sided swingarm and the mirror-chrome body. 0-100 km/h in about 3.4 s, top speed around 323 km/h.

The H2 has an up/down quickshifter: once you're rolling in gear, shift without the clutch. Pulling away still needs the clutch. It also has traction control, power modes (Full, Middle, Low) and ram air that adds a little power at high speed. Quickshifter and traction control can be switched off in the garage.
H2 sound: its own engine and parts profile, plus the supercharger whine that climbs with the revs and the chirp when you snap the throttle shut.

H2 garage: an H2R-style track kit (310 PS, 22 kg lighter, carbon wings, taller screen, open megaphone, no mirrors or plate), slicks, three paints, frame colour and the usual exhaust, carbon and suspension parts.
New H2 gauge: analog tachometer with an LCD showing speed, gear, fuel and a supercharger boost bar.

Multiplayer: when someone gets off their bike, everyone now sees it. Their bike stays parked with nobody on it and they walk around as a standing figure, with their name tag above their head. Riders on an older version still see the old way until they update.

Asking for a ride while you're on foot works now: walk up to a friend's bike, tap their name tag and hop on. Before, it left you half-walking with your bike hidden. GET OFF puts your own bike back down next to theirs.
If the driver gets off the bike, their passenger is let off too, and you can't ask to ride a bike whose rider has walked away. Races can't start while either of you is on foot.
Pinch to zoom, mouse-wheel zoom and the Field of view slider work again (since 11.38 the camera never picked up the FOV change, and leaving the garage could leave the view zoomed in).

Full-screen map: tap the minimap (or press M) and it opens out of the minimap's circle into a map of the whole island, with the game paused behind it. Drag to move (it coasts), pinch or scroll to zoom, a compass and a scale bar, named places, gas stations, quest pins and other riders. Esc, M or the X folds it back into the minimap.

Waypoints: tap anywhere on the land to drop a pin (it snaps to quest pins, gas stations and named places; the sea says no) and press SET WAYPOINT. A violet beacon marks it in the world, the minimap shows a pin or a rim arrow with the distance, and it clears itself when you arrive. CLEAR removes it. Not available during a race.
The second town (Poblacion Hilaga) is grey on the minimap like the first one.

The island is bigger: a small islet in the southern bay, reached by a causeway off the ring road (lighthouse, chapel, sari-sari store, fish stalls and resort cottages around its own loop road); a seaside resort strip with a boulevard, two resort hotels with pools, cottages and stalls along the new beach south of the ring road; a second town on the north coast (Poblacion Hilaga) with its own streets, shophouses, chapel and market stalls, joined to the ring road and the airstrip; and a harbor quay with warehouses, fish stalls and a lighthouse.

Ten new building types: two-storey house, bahay na bato, bungalow with a porch, sari-sari store (awning, sign, lit window), fish stall, resort cottage on a deck with a thatch roof, resort hotel with a pool, warehouse, chapel with a belfry and lit stained windows, and a lighthouse with a lamp that glows at night.

Map maker: the building brush has all the new types (paint the small ones like houses; chapel, lighthouse, warehouse and resort are placed one at a time) with width and depth fields for each. Palms no longer grow through buildings.

Options rebuilt: five tabs (Graphics, Controls, Audio, Game, System) with proper switches, segmented choices and sliders that show their real value, and a hint under every setting. Held sideways on a phone the tabs sit in a rail on the left so the settings get the full height.
One reload for all graphics changes: settings that rebuild the renderer are marked, saved, and applied together with one Apply & reload bar, instead of reloading the game after every tap.

Graphics presets (Performance / Balanced / Quality) set quality, anti-aliasing, sky lighting and auto resolution in one tap, and show Custom when you have changed one of them. Reset all options is in the System tab (two taps; your bikes and multiplayer name stay).

MSAA is back as an anti-aliasing choice next to FXAA: Off, FXAA, MSAA 2×, MSAA 4× or MSAA 4× + FXAA. It runs in the scene pass, so it works together with the colour grade and the N64 filter. WebGPU only has 4× samples (2× runs as 4×), and a GPU that cannot multisample falls back to FXAA and says so in Options. Your old FXAA on/off choice carries over.

Proper passengers on every bike, not just the tricycle: stop next to a friend's bike and tap their name tag (it shows 🏍️+1 when the pillion seat is free). RIDE asks, the driver taps OK, and you sit behind them. The passenger is the rider model again, shifted back onto the seat in different clothes (eight outfits, picked by player), so it costs one extra draw call and no new triangles.

The weight is real: 65 kg behind the rider moves the bike's centre of mass back and up, so it pulls away slower (a Raider 150 takes about 1.2 s longer to 60 km/h, a Smash 115 about 2.8 s), the front gets light and wheelies come earlier, braking distance is about the same. Taking the passenger off gives the bike back exactly.

First person looks over the driver's shoulder; GET OFF puts your own bike down on the driver's left. If the bike crashes, the passenger is flung out cartoon-style like the sidecar passengers. Switching bikes or fitting / removing the sidecar drops the passenger. A tricycle still seats two on the sidecar bench.
No relay update needed (the pillion uses the first entry of the same seat list). New: tools/pillion.mjs checks every bike's seat against the real model and plays a whole ride through a fake relay.

Cuter and lighter wheels: spokes, rim lip, hub, pinstripes and brake discs are now flat cut-out textures (N64 style) instead of little 3D parts. Every bike lost about 700-1,500 triangles (all eight together: 30.9k to 23.5k, a quarter of the bike geometry); the draw call count did not change.
The tyre is still a chunky 3D ring. The garage wheel colour, rim tape and carbon wheels still work, and brake discs now have drilled holes.
Faster: far fewer draw calls. Measured in five spots (lot, town, highway, town edge, plaza) on Medium: 115-180 draw calls per frame before, 26-35 now, with the same picture.

The ground is one object (every 280 m tile at every detail level, drawn nearest first), the roads are one per surface, and on WebGL 2 every prop of the island (houses, shops, roofs, trees, palms, poles, rails, parked vehicles, lamps...) is drawn once per material for the whole island instead of once per type per 700 m chunk. Untextured props and the church share one material, so most of the town is a single draw. All shadow-casting props are one draw in the shadow pass. Props now hide per 140 m cell instead of per 700 m chunk, so less off-screen geometry is drawn too.
Quest beacons are two draws in total (rings, beams) instead of 2-3 each; light pools are one, and pools and halos are skipped entirely by day (they were drawn invisible).
WebGPU keeps its GPU culling for props; the ground, roads, pools and beacons are batched there too. Not yet checked on a real phone.

Fixed: the mountain (terrace) road was buried. Where the road runs lower than the hillside, the grass climbed as a wall up to 17 m high within 5 m of the centre line, and the 5 m terrain mesh poked through the road surface, so the road was hard to see and you rode into invisible-looking walls. The ground beside a road now rises as a graded cut bank (at most 0.7 m per metre) behind a level shoulder, in bare earth colour so the road stands out against the grass, and no terrain reaches above the road surface any more.
Terrain below a road (embankments, bridges, river crossings) is unchanged. tools/roads.mjs now also checks the drawn mesh and the physics ground beside every road (CORRIDOR).

Fixed: bumps where roads meet. Every road used to be shaped on its own, so where two roads overlapped (crossings, branches, the town's north-east corner, the airstrip's taxi roads) they sat at different heights and the ground jumped between the two surfaces along the line where the nearest road changes: up to half a metre at the highway junctions. Now every junction is one level surface: the roads there share one height over the whole overlap and ease back into their own terrain-following profile at a gentle grade.
Fixed: the highway loop had a 6 cm step where its end met its start. It is now smoothed as a closed loop.
Fixed: a strip of ground inside a wide road could be treated as the shoulder of a narrower road next to it (a small lip). The road whose edge is nearest now decides.
The speed bumps are the only bumps left on the road: new tools/roads.mjs fails the test run if any junction, crossing or the loop seam has a step in it.

Fixed: the on-foot character was still drawn sitting down. The rider's parts are merged into one mesh when the bike is built, so the standing pose never kicked in. The body is now rebuilt standing (legs straight, torso upright, arms hanging) from the bike's own rider measurements.
On foot, first person: the walking bob is now Half-Life 1 style and much gentler: vertical only (no side sway, roll or wobble), one slow up-down per stride, height following your speed.

On foot, feel: the camera is much smoother (look angles ease, steps and slopes glide instead of popping, the third-person camera trails you softly and pulls back a little when you sprint), the body now stands upright instead of staying in the seated pose, and the first-person view has a proper walking bob, side sway and a faint breath when standing still.

On foot, movement: speed eases in and out with real friction instead of snapping, sprint builds up and drops off smoothly (with a slight widening of the view), turning around at speed is quick, and in first person backing up and strafing are slower. Jumping is more forgiving: you can still jump a moment after walking off an edge, a jump pressed just before landing counts, a tap is a short hop and holding the button jumps full height. Take-off and landing dip the camera, and a hard landing costs a little speed.
Fixed: KEY, KILL, START and BACK stayed on screen on touch devices while walking; they are now hidden whenever you are off the bike.
The main menu now has the garage look: dark frosted-glass panels, flat amber-highlight buttons and spaced amber headings. The island scene behind it is dimmed to match.
Fixed: the UPDATE button's version number was amber on amber and couldn't be read. (Menu theme by mrralphmc-ux, PR #1.)

Night lights: the light pools on the ground under lamp posts now follow the terrain (each pool is a small grid hugging the drawn ground) instead of a flat disc that floated over slopes and uneven ground.
On foot: CAM (or C) switches between first person (eyes at the helmet, no body) and third person.

On foot, touch controls: all the bike's controls are hidden and replaced by a joystick (push it all the way to run) and a JUMP button (hold to keep hopping); drag the screen to look around; GET OFF / GET ON now has its own free spot chosen by the layout solver, so it no longer sits on top of other buttons.

You can now get off the bike: F (or the GET OFF button when stopped) parks it with the key off and puts your rider on foot beside it. WASD walk, Shift run, Space jump, drag to look around; on touch the gas pad walks, the brake pad walks back, the wheel turns the camera and the up arrow jumps. You collide with buildings and the bike, can't wade into the sea, and F / GET ON next to the bike puts you back on it. Barebones for now: no animation, and other players still see your bike parked with its rider.
Fixed: the game didn't load in Firefox ("three" was not remapped).

Maps can now have extra islands, and every building is part of the map: roadside houses, nipa huts and shophouses are placed one by one, and the church, plaza, market, gas station and parking lot can be moved (the ground under them is levelled). Refuelling, parking quests and the spawn follow them.
The island's trees and palms were re-scattered once by this change.
The island is now loaded from swappable map files, ready for community-made map changes. Roads keep their own max grade when set.

Garage: the camera now frames the bike in the space the panels leave free (beside the panel in landscape, above it in portrait) and zooms to fit each bike's size, so the CBR, the scooters and the TMX with its tricycle sidecar are never cut off. Close-ups scale with the screen too; pinch / wheel zoom is relative.

Bike selection: the garage has a compact picker (‹ name ›, tap the name for a grid of all bikes) instead of rows of buttons. The title-screen bike list is a grid of cards with class, drivetrain, a power bar and weight.

Perf: the sun's shadow map is only redrawn when the light actually moves (it now follows the bike in ~3 m steps). Parked: no shadow pass at all; riding: a fraction of the frames. Shadows look the same.
Perf: GPU culling of the island props (trees, houses, posts...) is now one compute pass for all prop types instead of one per type, and is skipped entirely while the camera stands still.
Perf: all culling (distance, terrain detail, GPU props) now runs from one place each frame.
Fix: braking hard at speed could stand the bike on its nose and keep it there while the brake was held. The suspension now tops out, and lifting the rear wheel is left to the stoppie model.

Sound: silent layers (wind, tyre, brake, chain and ambience beds at zero volume) stop running on the audio thread until they are needed, and the engine voice idles when the engine is off or sound is muted. Less CPU and battery for the same sound.
Perf meter: cpu now reads game + draw time (e.g. 3.1+12.4 ms), and hitches caused by drawing are filed under draw instead of js.
New bike: Yamaha Aerox 155. 155 cc liquid-cooled VVA, 15.4 PS, CVT (2.300–0.724), 14" wheels, twin rear shocks, Stop & Start System.
New bike: Kawasaki Rouser NS125 Fi. 124 cc FI single, 12 PS, 5-speed, front disc / rear drum, 17" alloys, split seat.
New bike: Rusi Macho 125. 125 cc carb single, 9.7 hp, 5-speed, drum/drum, 17" spokes. Takes the tricycle sidecar in Parts.
Each new bike has its own sound profile (brakes, chain or belt, body rattle, starter).
New: WHAT'S NEW on the title screen shows these patch notes.
New: the game now checks for updates. When a newer build is out, an UPDATE button appears on the title screen and in the pause menu; one tap reloads into the new version (works with offline mode).
Tricycle rides: tap a trike's name tag (within 9 m, both stopped) to ask for a ride. Up to 2 passengers per trike, and each adds weight to the driver's physics.
Crashes fling passengers and the driver cartoon-style.
Sidecar windscreen is now transparent.
Multiplayer relay protocol update: ride messages need the relay redeployed.
New bike: TMX Supremo. 149 cc carb, 5-speed manual, drum brakes, 18" spoked wheels, twin-dial cluster.
Optional tricycle sidecar (Parts > Sidecar) with its own physics: no lean, pulls toward the sidecar on throttle, chair lift and rollover.
Fixed a frozen sound loop in the part sounds.
Part sounds: brake squeal, chain whirr and clunk, clutch rasp, suspension thump, body rattle, key clicks, exhaust ping, peg grind. Every bike has its own profile.
Grip-limited steering, wheelie control, smoother camera, regrip fix. Analog brake (11.4 - 11.6). Tyre model (11.2).
